A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work. Their main text, equations, figures and complete appendices support comparison, including matching results across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: V1 reports original quadratic simulations and neural-network experiments measuring accuracy, sharpness and variational objectives in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: V3 retains original empirical results and adds cross-entropy and SST-2 experiments in Appendix F.

M1.justification: The variational objective, Monte Carlo gradient averaging, and VON/IVON updates remain unchanged. Section 3 specializes the analyzed covariance to isotropic noise; the PDFs do not establish a changed training algorithm. Cross-entropy and BERT-mini are additional experimental settings.

E1.justification: Appendix F extends actual evaluation beyond quadratic simulations and image classification to SST-2 sentiment classification, using a trained classification head on frozen BERT-mini. This adds a distinct language domain and task while retaining CIFAR-10, SVHN and FashionMNIST.

E2.justification: The retained comparisons still use GD against VGD, Adam against adaptive IVON, and Gaussian perturbations against Student-t variants. The added cross-entropy and SST-2 experiments reuse GD controls; no new comparison method is introduced.

E3.justification: Appendix F adds cross-entropy training for a CIFAR-10 fully connected network and head-only SST-2 training on frozen BERT-mini, with learning rate 0.05 for both compared methods. Figure 9 additionally reports sharpness for the existing hyperparameter sweeps. These are limited protocol additions, without established revisions to retained experiments.

E4.justification: V3 adds an analysis of how cross-entropy changes sharpness dynamics and extends the learning-rate/batch-size analysis with sharpness curves. It removes v1 Figure 12's expanded quadratic variance-by-sample trajectory grid, while retaining related simulations and the existing posterior-tail, sample-count and eigenspectrum analyses.

E5.justification: V3's checklist newly states that experiments were averaged over various random seeds, without specifying their number or defining uncertainty estimates. This is additional reporting, not evidence of increased runs. The quadratic descent experiments retain their stated 10 trials.

E6.justification: V3 Figure 17 adds lower peak sharpness for fixed-covariance IVON versus GD under cross-entropy, and Figure 21 adds lower VGD sharpness on SST-2. Figure 9 adds hyperparameter-dependent sharpness results; v1 Figure 12's trajectory grid is removed. Retained benchmark and eigenspectrum results are otherwise preserved.

T1.justification: Section 3 narrows the stated covariance assumption from diagonal to isotropic, and Appendix B adds arguments about rank-deficient Hessians and initially zero gradient projections. Hypothesis 1 drops its explicit nonconvexity restriction. The variational-factor formula, concentration lemma and smoothing theorem remain substantially unchanged.

C1.justification: Both versions claim the first EoS analysis of variational learning, deriving a quadratic stability threshold and empirically linking posterior properties and sample counts to flatter solutions. The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain this central contribution; added experiments provide support rather than redefine it.

C2.justification: Appendix F newly explains cross-entropy sharpness decay through increasingly confident predictions and distinguishes lower transient peaks from eventual vanishing curvature. The introduction also explicitly acknowledges PAC-Bayes explanations of flatness and generalization. Existing qualifications about heavy-tailed and adaptive-method theory remain.

D1.justification: V3 adds a replication-code repository link absent from v1 and specifies the frozen BERT-mini backbone, trained head and shared SST-2 learning rate. Its checklist also states that a README documents the code. These add access and implementation information without establishing the repository's contents.

R1.justification: V3 adds Alquier et al. (2024) and explicitly positions PAC-Bayes theory as explaining why flatter solutions may generalize better. Appendix A also softens its characterization of earlier natural-gradient implementations. The broader related-work coverage and novelty positioning remain stable.

P1.justification: V3 substantially rewrites the abstract and main theoretical exposition, including the EoS background and stability-threshold explanation. It moves the SGD-noise comparison into Section 3.2, reorganizes the adaptive-method discussion and appends a NeurIPS checklist, while retaining the overall research narrative.

P2.justification: V3 adds the posterior-variance schematic in Figure 2 and empirical Figures 17 and 21, and expands Figure 9 with two sharpness panels. It removes v1 Figure 12, redraws the variance-sweep presentation and revises captions and figure placement. These are substantive display changes beyond renumbering.

improvement.justification: The cross-entropy and SST-2 experiments broaden empirical support, while the added sharpness panels make the hyperparameter argument more directly assessable. The replication-code link and revised exposition improve usability. These gains are limited by incomplete seed reporting and a new SST-2 reporting mismatch: Appendix F describes losses, whereas Figure 21 labels accuracy. The central theory and most evidence remain unchanged.
